section.content: 本发明涉及一种锂离子电池，其负极复合材料通过如下步骤制备得到：在50～70℃下，将硅烷前驱体、粘结剂、分散剂和水混合，搅拌反应5～15分钟，然后加入纳米硅粉，搅拌反应20～40分钟，然后调整反应体系的pH为3～4，在0～40℃下静置反应1.5～2.5小时，得到含有中间体颗粒的悬浮液；向悬浮液中加入石墨和/或针状焦，搅拌混合0.5～1.5小时，然后进行喷雾干燥，得到中间材料，其中，控制喷雾干燥的进口温度为210～320℃，出口温度为80～130℃；将中间材料在惰性气氛的保护下，在600～1200℃下进行氧化还原反应2～10小时，制得负极复合材料。本发明的锂离子电池的循环性能和库伦效率好。

The invention relates to a lithium ion battery, wherein a negative electrode composite material is prepared by the following steps: mixing a silane precursor, a binder, a dispersing agent and water at 50-70 ℃, stirring for reaction for 5-15 minutes, adding nano silicon powder, stirring for reaction for 20-40 minutes, adjusting the pH of a reaction system to 3-4, and standing for reaction for 1.5-2.5 hours at 0-40 ℃ to obtain a suspension containing intermediate particles; adding graphite and/or needle coke into the suspension, stirring and mixing for 0.5-1.5 hours, and then performing spray drying to obtain an intermediate material, wherein the inlet temperature of the spray drying is controlled to be 210-320 ℃, and the outlet temperature is controlled to be 80-130 ℃; and carrying out oxidation-reduction reaction on the intermediate material at 600-1200 ℃ for 2-10 hours under the protection of inert atmosphere to obtain the cathode composite material. The lithium ion battery has good cycle performance and coulombic efficiency.

Lithium ion battery

The invention relates to a split application of a lithium ion battery cathode composite material and a preparation method thereof, wherein the application date of the split application is 2017, 9 and 22, the application number of the split application is 2017108647988.

Technical Field

The invention relates to a lithium ion battery cathode composite material and a preparation method thereof.

Background

The negative electrode material is used as an important component of the lithium ion battery, the research objects of the negative electrode material are various, and the negative electrode material is mainly classified into two categories: the first is a carbon material, including graphitized carbon materials and amorphous carbon materials; the second category is non-carbon materials, mainly including silicon-based materials, tin-based materials, transition metal oxides, metal nitrides, other alloy negative electrode materials, and the like.

The ideal lithium ion battery cathode material should meet the following requirements:

1. the lithium ion battery has a lower oxidation-reduction potential so as to ensure that the lithium ion battery has higher output voltage;

2. a large amount of lithium ions can be allowed to be reversibly inserted and extracted, and the energy density is high;

3. the intercalation and deintercalation reaction of the lithium ions is highly reversible, and the change of the main structure is small, so that the lithium ion battery is ensured to have higher first efficiency and stable cycle performance;

4. the lithium ion battery has higher electronic conductivity and ionic conductivity, so that the electric polarization is reduced, and the lithium ion battery is ensured to have good high-current charge and discharge performance;

5. the lithium ion battery has no chemical reaction with the electrolyte, good compatibility and firm SEI protective film formed on the surface, thereby ensuring good safety and cycle performance of the lithium ion battery;

6. rich resources, low price and environmental protection.

Graphite is mostly adopted as a raw material for the current commercialized lithium ion battery cathode material, however, the theoretical capacity of natural graphite is 372mAh/g, the increasing demand of the current market for the high-energy density lithium ion battery cannot be met, and the development of a novel high-specific-capacity lithium ion battery cathode material is urgently needed. Each silicon atom can store up to 4.4 lithium atoms, so that the storage capacity reaches a theoretical value of 4200mAh/g, which is far higher than that of the current graphite, and the lithium removal potential platform is low, so that the silicon material becomes the negative electrode material of the lithium battery with the most development prospect at present. However, pure silicon undergoes a very large stress accompanied by a volume expansion of 300% during the reaction with lithium, resulting in pulverization of the brittle silicon electrode and deterioration of cycle stability. Therefore, in order to apply silicon to a commercial lithium ion battery, the problem of volume expansion of silicon during charge and discharge must be solved.

For example, CN104953122A discloses a nano silicon carbon composite anode material and a preparation method thereof, the anode material is a core-shell structure, a gap exists between the outer wall of the core and the inner wall of the shell, the core is made of nano silicon, and the shell is a nano porous carbon layer, the preparation method comprises the following steps:

mixing the nano silicon particlesCalcining and oxidizing at 700-1000 ℃ in an oxygen-containing atmosphere to obtain SiO2Coated nano-silicon particles;

mixing nano SiO2Particles of said SiO2Dissolving the coated nano silicon particles, a dispersing agent and an organic carbon source in a solvent for dispersion treatment, and then performing spray drying treatment to obtain the nano embedded SiO2The surface-oxidized nano-silicon particles coated with organic carbon of (a), the surface-oxidized nano-silicon particles being the SiO2Coated nano-silicon particles;

will be embedded with nano SiO2The organic carbon-coated surface oxidized nano silicon particles are subjected to thermal cracking reaction in an oxygen-free atmosphere, so that an organic carbon source is cracked into amorphous carbon to obtain the nano SiO-embedded nano silicon dioxide2The amorphous carbon coated surface oxidized nano silicon particles of (a);

will be embedded with nano SiO2The amorphous carbon coated surface oxidized nano silicon particles are placed in HF solution for reaction, and the nano SiO is removed2And oxidizing the surface of the nano-particles to generate the nano-silicon-carbon composite anode material of nano-silicon coated by the nano-porous carbon layer.

The cathode material prepared by the patent has good battery cycling stability, but the preparation method is complex.

In addition, the prior art also includes the following schemes: and (2) carrying out ball milling and intermixing on the simple substance silicon and the silicon monoxide, then carrying out spray drying on the mixture of the simple substance silicon and the graphite, carrying out asphalt coating on the obtained spheroidal particles, and calcining the spheroidal particles in an inert atmosphere to obtain the silicon dioxide. However, this solution has the following drawbacks: simple substance silicon and silicon monoxide are only simply physically mixed, the particle size of the finally generated particles is micron-sized, and then the particles are mixed with graphite and then coated with amorphous carbon. Because the material has larger particles, the previous coating layer can be damaged by volume expansion in the charging and discharging processes, so that the electrode is pulverized, and the cycling stability is poor.

Disclosure of Invention

The invention aims to provide a lithium ion battery with good cycle performance.

In order to solve the technical problems, the invention adopts the following technical scheme:

a lithium ion battery comprises a negative electrode, wherein the negative electrode comprises a negative electrode composite material, and the negative electrode composite material is prepared by the following steps:

mixing a silane precursor, a binder, a dispersing agent and water at 50-70 ℃, stirring for 5-15 minutes, adding nano silicon powder, stirring for 20-40 minutes, adjusting the pH of a reaction system to 3-4, and standing for 1.5-2.5 hours at 0-40 ℃ to obtain a suspension containing intermediate particles;

adding graphite and/or needle coke into the suspension obtained by the reaction in the step (1), stirring and mixing for 0.5-1.5 hours, and then performing spray drying to obtain an intermediate material, wherein the inlet temperature of the spray drying is controlled to be 210-320 ℃, and the outlet temperature is controlled to be 80-130 ℃;

and (3) carrying out redox reaction on the intermediate material prepared in the step (2) at 600-1200 ℃ for 2-10 hours under the protection of inert atmosphere to prepare the cathode composite material.

Preferably, the mass ratio of the silane precursor, the binder, the dispersing agent, the nano silicon powder, the graphite and/or the needle coke is 0.4-0.6: 0.05-0.1: 0.03-0.06: 1: 0.5 to 1, and more preferably 0.4 to 0.6: 0.05-0.1: 0.03-0.05: 1: 0.9 to 1, more preferably 0.5 to 0.6: 0.09-0.1: 0.03-0.05: 1: 0.9 to 1.

Preferably, the feeding mass ratio of the nano silicon powder to the water is 1: 1.5 to 2.5, and more preferably 1: 1.8-2.2, more preferably 1: 1.9 to 2.1.

Preferably, the silane precursor is selected from methyltrimethoxysilane, ethyltriethoxysilane or ethyltrimethoxysilane.

Preferably, the binder is one or more selected from hydroxyethyl cellulose, polyvinyl alcohol, polyvinylpyrrolidone and sodium carboxymethyl cellulose.

Further preferably, the adhesive is prepared from the following components in a mass ratio of 1: 4-8 of a mixture of hydroxyethyl cellulose and polyvinyl alcohol.

More preferably, the binder is a mixture of 1: 4-5 of a mixture of hydroxyethyl cellulose and polyvinyl alcohol.

Preferably, the dispersant is one or more selected from the group consisting of an aqueous wetting agent, a fluorine-containing active agent and sodium dodecyl benzene sulfonate.

Preferably, the particle size (D50) of the nano silicon powder is 50-100 nm.

In the invention, the nano silicon powder is prepared by adopting a plasma method, and preferably, the nano silicon powder is purchased from S100 of Jinyi silicon material development Co., Ltd, Chongqing.

Preferably, the graphite is one or more selected from artificial graphite, intermediate phase graphite and natural graphite.

Preferably, the D50 of the graphite is 1-10 microns.

Preferably, in step (1), the pH is controlled by dropwise addition of nitric acid.

Preferably, the particle size of the intermediate particles prepared in step (1) is 0.6-2 microns, and more preferably 0.6-1 micron.

Preferably, the specific implementation manner of step (1) is: mixing a silane precursor, a binder, a dispersing agent and water at 55-65 ℃, stirring and reacting for 8-12 minutes, adding nano silicon powder, stirring and reacting for 25-35 minutes, adjusting the pH of a reaction system to 3-4, and standing and reacting for 1.8-2.2 hours at 10-30 ℃ to obtain a suspension containing intermediate particles.

Preferably, the specific implementation manner of step (2) is: adding graphite into the suspension obtained by the reaction in the step (1), stirring and mixing for 0.8-1.2 hours, and then performing spray drying to obtain an intermediate material, wherein the inlet temperature of the spray drying is controlled to be 280-300 ℃, and the outlet temperature of the spray drying is controlled to be 100-120 ℃.

Preferably, the specific implementation manner of step (3) is: and (3) carrying out redox reaction on the intermediate material prepared in the step (2) at 1000-1200 ℃ for 4-8 hours under the protection of inert atmosphere to prepare the lithium ion battery cathode composite material.

Preferably, the inert atmosphere in step (3) is nitrogen or argon.

Preferably, the negative electrode composite material comprises a core body, an intermediate layer which is coated outside the core body and has pores, and an outer layer coated outside the intermediate layer; the core body is nano silicon, the middle layer is silicon monoxide compounded with graphite and/or needle coke, and the outer layer is amorphous carbon.

More preferably, the porosity of the intermediate layer is 0.1% to 5%.

More preferably, the particle size of the nano silicon is 50-100 nm.

Preferably, the negative electrode is prepared by mixing the negative electrode composite material, the conductive agent and the adhesive and then coating the mixture on a negative electrode pole piece.

Further preferably, the negative electrode plate is a copper foil.

Preferably, the lithium ion battery is a button cell battery.

The principle of the invention is that nano-silicon is used as a precursor core, and the silica is used as a coating shell by a sol-gel method to form a porous core-shell structure, the structure provides a certain space to control the volume expansion of nano-silicon particles in the charging and discharging processes, and simultaneously, the silica is compounded with graphite, and the outermost layer is coated with amorphous carbon, thereby greatly improving the cycle stability.

Due to the implementation of the technical scheme, compared with the prior art, the invention has the following advantages:

according to the invention, through improvement of the preparation method, the cathode composite material with a novel structure is obtained, the cathode composite material can control the volume expansion of silicon in a certain space, effectively prevent pulverization of a silicon electrode, improve the cycle stability, and can be used as a cathode material of a high-capacity lithium battery, thereby improving the cycle performance and the coulombic efficiency of the lithium ion battery. The preparation method has simple process and is suitable for industrial production.

Drawings

Fig. 1 is a first charge-discharge curve of a lithium battery manufactured from the negative electrode material of example 1.

Detailed Description

The present invention will be described in further detail with reference to specific examples. It is to be understood that these embodiments are provided to illustrate the basic principles, essential features and advantages of the present invention, and the present invention is not limited by the following embodiments. The implementation conditions used in the examples can be further adjusted according to specific requirements, and the implementation conditions not indicated are generally the conditions in routine experiments. Not indicated, "%" is mass percent. The raw materials in the invention are all available in the market.

Example 1

(1) Adding 500g of methyltrimethoxysilane into 20Kg of aqueous solution containing 20g of HEC, 80g of PVA and 50g of DISPEBYK-2012, stirring and reacting for 10min, adding 1Kg of nano silicon powder (50-100 nm of D50), stirring and reacting for 30min, and controlling the temperature at 60 ℃. Dropwise adding nitric acid, controlling the pH value to be 3-4, standing and reacting for 2h at normal temperature (25 ℃), and obtaining an intermediate (Si/SiO)x)，D50＝800nm。

(2) 1Kg of graphite (D50 ═ 10 um) was added to the above suspension system, stirred and mixed for 1 hour, and spray-dried, with the inlet temperature of the spray dryer set at 300 ℃ and the outlet temperature set at 120 ℃ to give a spheroidal material.

(3) And (3) carrying out oxidation-reduction reaction and carbonization treatment on the spheroidal material in a carbonization furnace under the argon atmosphere, setting the temperature at 1200 ℃, and keeping the temperature for 4 hours to obtain the modified spheroidal material.

Example 2

(1) Adding 400g of methyltrimethoxysilane into 20Kg of aqueous solution containing 10g of HEC, 40g of PVA and 30g of DISPEBYK-2012, stirring and reacting for 10min, adding 1Kg of nano silicon powder (50-100 nm of D50), stirring and reacting for 30min, and controlling the temperature at 60 ℃. Dropwise adding nitric acid, controlling the pH value to be 3-4, standing and reacting for 2h at normal temperature (25 ℃), and obtaining an intermediate (Si/SiO)x)，D50＝600nm。

(2) 1Kg of D50 ═ 10um graphite was added to the suspension system, stirred and mixed for 1 hour, and spray-dried, with the inlet temperature of the spray dryer set at 280 ℃ and the outlet temperature at 110 ℃ to give a spheroidal material.

(3) And (3) carrying out oxidation-reduction reaction and carbonization treatment on the spheroidal material in a carbonization furnace under the argon atmosphere, setting the temperature at 1200 ℃, and keeping the temperature for 4 hours to obtain the modified spheroidal material.

Example 3

(1) Adding 600g of methyltrimethoxysilane into 20Kg of aqueous solution containing 20g of HEC, 80g of PVA and 30g of DISPEBYK-2012, stirring and reacting for 10min, adding 1Kg of nano silicon powder (D50 is 50-100 nm), stirring and reacting for 30min, and controlling the temperature at 60 ℃. Dropwise adding nitric acid, controlling the pH value to be 3-4, standing and reacting for 2h at normal temperature (25 ℃), and obtaining an intermediate (Si/SiO)x)，D50＝1um。

(2) Graphite of 900-1 um in 900g D50 was added to the suspension system and stirred for 1 hour to spray dry, with the inlet temperature of the spray dryer set at 280 ℃ and the outlet temperature set at 100 ℃ to give a spheroidal material.

(3) And (3) carrying out oxidation-reduction reaction and carbonization treatment on the spheroidal material in a carbonization furnace under the argon atmosphere, setting the temperature to be 1000 ℃, and keeping the temperature for 8 hours to obtain the modified spheroidal material.

Example 4

(1) Adding 500g of methyltrimethoxysilane into 20Kg of aqueous solution containing 10g of HEC, 80g of PVA and 60g of DISPEBYK-2012, stirring and reacting for 10min, adding 1Kg of nano silicon powder (D50 is 50-100 nm), stirring and reacting for 30min, and controlling the temperature at 60 ℃. Dropwise adding nitric acid, controlling the pH value to be 3-4, standing and reacting for 2h at normal temperature (25 ℃), and obtaining an intermediate (Si/SiO)x)，D50＝800nm。

(2) 1Kg of graphite, 1um from D50, was added to the suspension system and stirred for 1 hour to spray dry, with the inlet temperature of the spray dryer set at 300 ℃ and the outlet temperature set at 90 ℃ to give a spheroidal material.

(3) And (3) carrying out oxidation-reduction reaction and carbonization treatment on the spheroidal material in a carbonization furnace under the nitrogen atmosphere, setting the temperature to be 800 ℃, and keeping the temperature for 4 hours to obtain the modified spheroidal material.

Example 5

(1) 500g methyltrimethoxysilane was added to 20Kg of an aqueous solution containing 20g HEC, 80g PVA, and 50g DISPEBYK-2012, the reaction was stirred for 10min, and 1Kg (D5) was added0 is 50-100 nm), stirring and reacting for 30min, and controlling the temperature at 60 ℃. Dropwise adding nitric acid, controlling the pH value to be 3-4, standing and reacting for 2h at normal temperature (25 ℃), and obtaining an intermediate (Si/SiO)x)，D50＝800nm。

(2) Graphite of 500g D50 ═ 1um was added to the suspension system, and the mixture was stirred and mixed for 1 hour, followed by spray drying, the inlet temperature of the spray dryer was set to 280 ℃ and the outlet temperature was set to 90 ℃ to obtain a spheroidal material.

(3) And (3) carrying out oxidation-reduction reaction and carbonization treatment on the spheroidal material in a carbonization furnace under the nitrogen atmosphere, setting the temperature at 800 ℃, and keeping the temperature for 6 hours to obtain the modified spheroidal material.

Comparative example 1

(1) Adding 500g of methyltrimethoxysilane into 20Kg of aqueous solution containing 20g of HEC, 80g of PVA and 50g of DISPEBYK-2012, stirring and reacting for 10min, adding 1Kg of nano silicon powder (50-100 nm of D50), stirring and reacting for 30min, and controlling the temperature at 60 ℃. Dropwise adding nitric acid, controlling the pH value to be 3-4, standing and reacting for 2h at normal temperature (25 ℃), and obtaining an intermediate (Si/SiO)x)，D50＝800nm。

(2) And (3) carrying out oxidation-reduction reaction and carbonization treatment on the intermediate in a carbonization furnace under the argon atmosphere, setting the temperature at 1200 ℃, and keeping the temperature for 4 hours to obtain the intermediate.

Comparative example 2

(1) 1Kg (50-100 nm of D50) of silica powder is added into 20Kg of aqueous solution containing 20g of HEC, 80g of PVA and 50g of DISPEBYK-2012, and 1Kg of graphite with the diameter of 1um D50 is added and stirred uniformly. Spray drying was carried out with the inlet temperature of the spray dryer set to 250 ℃ and the outlet temperature set to 90 ℃ to obtain a spheroidal material.

(3) And (3) carbonizing the spheroidal material in a carbonization furnace in nitrogen atmosphere, and keeping the temperature at 600 ℃ for 4 hours to obtain the modified spheroidal material.

And (3) performance testing:

directly mixing the carbon-based negative electrode composite material with the core-shell structure of nano silicon and silica oxide, the conductive agent and the binder in the mass percentages of 70:15:15 of the above examples 1-5 and comparative examples 1-2, fully stirring, coating a copper foil with the thickness of 20um and the scraper of 100um, drying, rolling, slicing, and making a poleThe diameter of the sheet is 13mm, and the electrolyte is EC/DEC (volume ratio of 1:1) and 1MLiPF6The CR2032 button cell was assembled in an inert gas glove box. The test instrument is CT2001A of blue-electron limited company in Wuhan; the test procedure is that the temperature is changed into 3 circles at 0.05C/0.05C, the charge and the discharge are carried out for 5 circles at 0.1C/0.1C, and the cycle is carried out for 800 circles at 0.2C/0.2C; the charge and discharge voltage is 0.01V-1V.

The first charge-discharge curve of the button cell prepared by using the carbon-based negative electrode composite material with the nano-silicon and sub-silicon oxide core-shell structure in example 1 as an electrode is shown in fig. 1.

Table 1 shows the results of the performance tests of examples 1 to 5 and comparative examples 1 to 2.

As can be seen from Table 1 and FIG. 1, the discharge capacity of the carbon-based negative electrode composite material with the core-shell structure of nano-silicon and silica is higher and can reach more than 800 mAh/g. The material used as the lithium ion battery cathode material has good cycle performance, the capacity retention rate after 500 charge-discharge cycles is more than 82%, and the capacity retention rate after 500 charge-discharge cycles of the material in the comparative example is only about 70%.
